botanical.title: The Science of the Pistachio Tree
botanical.latinSubtitle: Pistacia vera L. — Resilient Mediterranean Specimen
botanical.subtitle: A resilient Mediterranean species engineered by nature for longevity and value.
botanical.desc: The pistachio (*Pistacia vera*) is uniquely suited to arid climates, possessing a deep taproot and low humidity requirements. Success in commercial production depends upon matching the right rootstock with appropriate female and male cultivars.
botanical.card1Desc: Exceptional physiological tolerance to high summer temperatures, low atmospheric moisture, and extreme dry conditions.
botanical.card2Desc: Requires specific winter chilling accumulation to break dormancy evenly, with variety selection tailored to regional climatic zones.
botanical.card3Desc: Sustained global market expansion driven by premium plant-based protein content, healthy lipids, and high economic yields per hectare.

Recognizing the transformative potential of pistachios in arid terrains, we concentrated all efforts on mastering rootstock genetics and grafting techniques.

expertise.title: Specialized Agronomic Knowledge
expertise.lead: Real experience in the field informs every plant we produce.
expertise.p1: Pistachio cultivation is a precise science: soil texture, active limestone, water electrical conductivity, and seasonal chill hours dictate the viability of every orchard. Our team provides realistic, factual recommendations based on field realities.
expertise.p2: We do not simply produce plants; we execute land preparation, precision GPS planting, and field grafting across multiple regions. This continuous feedback loop between nursery propagation and field results guarantees superior quality.

intro.title: Nursery Plant Material & Rootstocks
intro.desc: We supply professional plant material suited for diverse planting windows, soil compositions, and agricultural management styles.

ucb1.title: UCB1 Hybrid Rootstock
ucb1.subtitle: Pistacia atlantica × Pistacia integerrima
ucb1.desc: The UCB1 hybrid is the predominant rootstock for modern commercial pistachio farming worldwide. Bred for superior vigor and disease tolerance, it offers exceptional performance in irrigated and fertile soils.
ucb1.feat1Desc: Accelerated trunk caliper development and canopy expansion, leading to earlier commercial framework formation.
ucb1.feat2Desc: Demonstrated resistance to low winter temperatures, suitable for continental Mediterranean winter conditions.
ucb1.feat3Desc: Proven capacity to thrive in soils and water supplies with elevated sodium and boron concentrations.
ucb1.feat4Desc: Higher tolerance against soil-borne Verticillium dahliae wilt compared to traditional terebinthus.
ucb1.formatNote: Available in containerized pots, forestry alveoles, and as dormant bare-root rootstocks.

traditional.title: Hardy Mediterranean Rootstocks
traditional.subtitle: Natural resilience for dry-land and limestone soils.
traditional.cornicabraDesc: The native Mediterranean rootstock par excellence. Renowned for its extreme rusticity, Cornicabra develops a deep, vertical taproot system that searches for moisture in rocky, limestone-rich, and non-irrigated dry-land terrains.
traditional.cornicabraPoint1: Unmatched drought resistance in rainfed conditions
traditional.cornicabraPoint2: Thrives in stony, poor, and highly calcareous soils
traditional.cornicabraPoint3: High longevity and excellent graft compatibility
traditional.atlanticaDesc: A highly resilient rootstock adapted to semi-arid climates. It features great tolerance to limestone soils and dry conditions, developing a strong and extensive root network.
traditional.atlanticaPoint1: Strong root penetration in compact soils
traditional.atlanticaPoint2: High resistance to summer heat and drought
traditional.atlanticaPoint3: Traditional graft base with proven Mediterranean history

grafted.title: Grafted Pistachio Plants
grafted.desc: Professionally grafted pistachio plants with verified varietal scions budded onto selected rootstocks. We prepare plants in two distinct formats to accommodate different planting seasons and soil conditions.
grafted.potDesc: Grown in specialized nursery pots with structured root balls. Allows for flexible planting schedules throughout spring, autumn, and mild winter periods without transplant shock.
grafted.potPoint2: Extended planting window throughout the season
grafted.bareDesc: Supplied during winter vegetative dormancy. Ideal for large-scale commercial plantations established between December and March, facilitating efficient handling and transport.
grafted.barePoint2: Direct soil integration during natural winter dormancy

varieties.title: Pistachio Varieties & Pollinators
varieties.desc: Pistachio trees are dioecious, requiring female fruit-bearing trees and compatible male pollinator trees planted in proximity. A standard commercial ratio is 1 male tree for every 8 to 10 female trees.
varieties.kermanDesc: The most widely recognized female variety globally. Produces large, round nuts with an ivory shell and high commercial market acceptance. Requires approximately 800-1000 winter chill hours and flowers late, avoiding early spring frosts.
varieties.siroraDesc: Developed in Australia, Sirora is distinguished by its rapid vegetative growth, intermediate flowering date, and high percentage of naturally split shells. Highly productive and well-adapted to varied Mediterranean conditions.
varieties.larnakaDesc: An early-flowering variety originating in Cyprus. Produces elongated nuts with an exceptionally green kernel and intense aromatic profile, making it the preferred choice for confectionery, pastry, and artisanal gelato.
varieties.pollinatorsDesc: Male cultivars do not produce fruit but provide crucial pollen. Peter matches the late flowering period of Kerman, while Guerrero and early males provide synchronized pollen for Sirora and Larnaka.
